title: A model-provider error leaves the turn silent instead of showing a failure
description: 2026-10-04 on develop.chattic.us: a message to the Ping bot (sent by voice, but the path is the ordinary POST /messages turn) got no reply. The ComputerlessWorker logged OpenAI 429 Too Many Requests twice (HTTPStatusError from openai_completion.py:308 via computerless.py:386, raised out of lambda_handler.py:138). The member saw nothing: no failure, no retry notice. Expected: the turn ends visibly as failed with a readable reason (for example 'The model provider refused the request: quota exceeded'), per the turn recovery features. Root cause of the 429 itself is the OpenAI account being out of credits (also breaks Kanbus summaries and the live OpenAI pytest tests).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Trace (2026-10-04): openai_completion.py:308 raise_for_status escapes ComputerlessWorker.run_job (computerless.py:386) and lambda_handler.py:138 -- no classification, no turn.failed. SQS (TurnJobs, no DLQ, no maxReceiveCount, no reportBatchItemFailures) redelivers every ~180s. Only the deadline watchdog fails the turn (~5 min) with 'recovery attempts exhausted'. Web: on turn.failed the bubble is cleared (shouldClearTurnBubbleAfterTerminal) and the reason is small streamError text with Dismiss only; reload shows nothing (GET /channels/{id}/turn 404s for non-active turns, no message row). Plan: (1) worker classifies provider errors (insufficient_quota/401/400 permanent; other 429/5xx/timeouts retryable, bounded) and fails the turn immediately with code + readable reason via a fenced worker endpoint; (2) UI keeps a failed bubble with the reason and Retry, also after reload.

right_now_summary: The worker must classify provider errors and show a readable failure with retry guidance instead of leaving the turn
